# Project plan

## Start-up phase
<!--

 - [ ] Setting up collaboration platform inc. code for contributors etc.

The project will be developed in a public GitHub repository under the MIT licence, with issues used to track all work.

## Technical delivery
<!--
Covering the actual delivery of the project this section should
provide at least a high-level description of the implementation.

Including target dates is really important as you need to be committed
and the ISC need to have a means of tracking delivery
-->

Initial experiments running Vale over an existing R package confirm that it extracts comments from R source files with correct line numbers and handles vignettes and READMEs without any additional work.
They also show that its built-in styles are noisy on R code, with most reported problems being function and argument names flagged as spelling errors, which is what an R-specific style and vocabulary will address.

### Milestone 1 - 31st January 2027: working package and first rules

Consultation with package maintainers and a review of documentation feedback in public software review threads, such as rOpenSci's, to decide which rules will be most useful in the default style.
The code delivered is the R package which installs or locates Vale, runs it over a package, and returns lints as a data frame, with an initial set of rules and snapshot tests, working on Linux, macOS and Windows.

### Milestone 2 - 28th February 2027: default style, release and GitHub Action

The remaining rules, the vocabulary of R terms, config file generation and JSON output, each rule documented with examples of passes and failures.
A run over the 100 most downloaded CRAN packages drives tuning of the rules and defaults.
The package is submitted to CRAN, the style is published so that it can be installed directly by Vale users, and a GitHub Action and pre-commit hook are released so that linting can run on CI, together with a command that writes the active rules into a project's AGENTS.md file.
A post on the R Consortium blog reports on the project.

## Other aspects

All code is MIT licensed and developed in the open on GitHub. The package will be submitted to CRAN and the style published on GitHub so that it can be used with Vale directly.
The work will be publicised with a post on the R Consortium blog, posts on LinkedIn, Mastodon and Bluesky at each milestone, and submission to R Weekly.

The budget is labour only, at USD 90 per hour, covering 50 hours of part-time work over two months.
There are no other costs, as the project uses GitHub for hosting, CI and releases.

| Milestone | Target | Hours | USD |
|-----------|--------|------:|----:|
| 1: Working package and first rules | 31 Jan 2027 | 30 | 2,700 |
| 2: Default style, release and GitHub Action | 28 Feb 2027 | 20 | 1,800 |
| **Total** | | **50** | **4,500** |
